name: Asa in his first years
charge: Taking away the strange altars and the high places; commanding Judah to seek the Lord and do the law; crying to the Lord against a million Ethiopians
summary: Before the failure that is its own case, Asa did thirty-five years of what a king was for. He removed the idols, removed his own mother from being queen for her grove, made Judah swear to seek the Lord with all their heart, and when Zerah came against him with a million men he prayed one prayer and won.
offense: Asa removed the strange altars and images and commanded Judah to seek the Lord and do His law. He used the years of quiet to strengthen the cities, acknowledging that their rest came from seeking God. When Zerah came against him with an overwhelming army, Asa did not measure deliverance by numbers. He cried to the Lord, with whom it is nothing to help with many or with those who have no power. After the victory, Azariah called the king and people to continued faithfulness: the Lord would be with them while they were with Him. Asa took courage, renewed the altar, and gathered the people into a covenant to seek God with all their heart. He removed Maachah from being queen because of her idol, allowing neither family position nor royal privilege to shelter the abomination.
judgment: The Lord defeated the Ethiopians before Asa, and Judah returned with spoil. Others gathered to Asa when they saw that the Lord was with him. The people rejoiced in the oath they had made, sought God with their whole desire, and found Him. He gave them rest round about. The strength of this beginning lay in dependence upon God, not simply in fortified walls or military success. The same word that encouraged Asa also warned him that forsaking the Lord would have consequences.

entries.commentary: Abijah sleeps with his fathers and Asa his son reigns; the land is quiet ten years. Asa does that which is good and right, taking away the altars of the strange gods, the high places, the images, and the groves. Asa commands Judah to seek the Most High and to do the law and the commandment. The pattern of Rehoboam warns what happens when a strong king forsakes that law. -

Asa builds fenced cities because the land has rest and no war, for the Most High has given him rest. Rest is not idleness; while the land is before them they build walls, towers, gates, and bars. Asa has an army of 300,000 of Judah and 280,000 of Benjamin, all mighty men of valor. -

Zerah the Ethiopian, a Cushite, comes out with a host of a thousand thousand and three hundred chariots. Asa cries unto the Most High that it is nothing for him to help with many or with them that have no power. The Most High smites the Ethiopians before Asa; they flee and are destroyed, and Judah carries away very much spoil. Faith in the Most High, not the numbers of the enemy, wins the battle. -

The fear of the Most High comes on all the cities round about Gerar, and Judah spoils them, for there was exceeding much spoil in them. They smite the tents of cattle and carry away sheep and camels in abundance, then return to Jerusalem.

The Spirit of God comes on Azariah the son of Oded, who meets Asa and says the Most High is with them while they are with him; if they seek him he will be found, but if they forsake him he will forsake them. Israel had long been without the true God, a teaching priest, and law, but when in their trouble they turned to the Most High, he was found of them. Azariah charges Asa to be strong, for his work shall be rewarded.

When Asa hears these words and the prophecy of Oded, he takes courage, puts away the abominable idols out of Judah, Benjamin, and the cities he took from mount Ephraim, and renews the altar of the Most High. Hearing the word gives courage still, for we teach our people who they are, that the Israelites and the Christ are black. Faith comes by hearing. -

Asa gathers Judah, Benjamin, and the strangers out of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon, who fell to him in abundance when they saw the Most High was with him. These strangers are Israelites whose hearts turned back. In the fifteenth year of Asa they enter a covenant to seek the Most High with all their heart and soul, that whosoever would not seek him should be put to death. They swear with a loud voice, and the Most High gives them rest round about.

Asa removes Maachah his mother from being queen because she made an idol in a grove; he cuts it down, stamps it, and burns it at the brook Kidron. Though the high places are not all taken away, the heart of Asa is perfect all his days. He brings the dedicated silver, gold, and vessels into the house of God, and there is no more war until the thirty and fifth year of his reign.

Abijam reigns three years in Jerusalem and walks in all the sins of his father, his heart not perfect with the Most High as David's was. The children did what they saw their fathers do, not merely what was said, which is why the Most High teaches His people to be different. Yet for David's sake the Most High gives him a lamp in Jerusalem, because David did right all his days save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite, a wrong from which David repented. -

After Abijam dies, Asa his son reigns forty-one years and does right in the eyes of the Most High as David his father did. Asa takes the sodomites out of the land, removes the idols his fathers made, and even removes his own mother Maachah from being queen because she made an idol in a grove, which he destroys and burns at the brook Kidron. Though the high places are not removed, Asa's heart is perfect with the Most High all his days, and he brings dedicated silver, gold, and vessels into the house of the Most High.

There is war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel, who builds Ramah to cut off passage to and from Asa. Asa takes silver and gold from the house of the Most High and the king's house and sends it to Benhadad of Syria to break his league with Baasha, and Benhadad smites cities of Israel so Baasha stops building Ramah. Asa uses the stones and timber of Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah. In his old age he is diseased in his feet, then sleeps with his fathers, and Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his place.

Nadab son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel two years and does evil, walking in the way and sin of his father. Baasha conspires against him, kills him, and reigns in his place, then smites all the house of Jeroboam, leaving none that breathed, according to the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite. This fulfills, years later, the judgment that Jeroboam's descendants would be destroyed for the sins by which he made Israel to sin.

Baasha reigns twenty-four years in Tirzah and does evil, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin by which he made Israel to sin. The pattern continues: each king who follows takes up the sin of the one before, and the same judgments keep coming.

verses.text: So Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his stead. In his days the land was quiet ten years.
And Asa did that which was good and right in the eyes of the Lord his God:
For he took away the altars of the strange gods, and the high places, and brake down the images, and cut down the groves:
And commanded Judah to seek the Lord God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.
Also he took away out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the images: and the kingdom was quiet before him.
And he built fenced cities in Judah: for the land had rest, and he had no war in those years; because the Lord had given him rest.

Therefore he said unto Judah, Let us build these cities, and make about them walls, and towers, gates, and bars, while the land is yet before us; because we have sought the Lord our God, we have sought him, and he hath given us rest on every side. So they built and prospered.
And there came out against them Zerah the Ethiopian with an host of a thousand thousand, and three hundred chariots; and came unto Mareshah.
Then Asa went out against him, and they set the battle in array in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

And Asa cried unto the Lord his God, and said, Lord, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Lord our God; for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude. O Lord, thou art our God; let not man prevail against thee.
So the Lord smote the Ethiopians before Asa, and before Judah; and the Ethiopians fled.

And Asa and the people that were with him pursued them unto Gerar: and the Ethiopians were overthrown, that they could not recover themselves; for they were destroyed before the Lord, and before his host; and they carried away very much spoil.
And they smote all the cities round about Gerar; for the fear of the Lord came upon them: and they spoiled all the cities; for there was exceeding much spoil in them.
They smote also the tents of cattle, and carried away sheep and camels in abundance, and returned to Jerusalem.
And the Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded:

And he went out to meet Asa, and said unto him, Hear ye me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin; The Lord is with you, while ye be with him; and if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you.
Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without law.
But when they in their trouble did turn unto the Lord God of Israel, and sought him, he was found of them.
And in those times there was no peace to him that went out, nor to him that came in, but great vexations were upon all the inhabitants of the countries.
And nation was destroyed of nation, and city of city: for God did vex them with all adversity.
Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.

And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim, and renewed the altar of the Lord, that was before the porch of the Lord.
And they entered into a covenant to seek the Lord God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul;
That whosoever would not seek the Lord God of Israel should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.
And they sware unto the Lord with a loud voice, and with shouting, and with trumpets, and with cornets.
And all Judah rejoiced at the oath: for they had sworn with all their heart, and sought him with their whole desire; and he was found of them: and the Lord gave them rest round about.

And also concerning Maachah the mother of Asa the king, he removed her from being queen, because she had made an idol in a grove: and Asa cut down her idol, and stamped it, and burnt it at the brook Kidron.
But the high places were not taken away out of Israel: nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days.
And he brought into the house of God the things that his father had dedicated, and that he himself had dedicated, silver, and gold, and vessels.
And there was no more war unto the five and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa.
And Asa did that which was right in the eyes of the Lord, as did David his father.
And he took away the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.
And also Maachah his mother, even her he removed from being queen, because she had made an idol in a grove; and Asa destroyed her idol, and burnt it by the brook Kidron.
But the high places were not removed: nevertheless Asa’s heart was perfect with the Lord all his days.
And he brought in the things which his father had dedicated, and the things which himself had dedicated, into the house of the Lord, silver, and gold, and vessels.
